  13  # class to TinyDB. Currently, this supports PyCharm, Pyright/VS Code and MyPy.
  14  TableBase: type[Table] = with_typehint(Table)
  15  
  16  
  17  class TinyDB(TableBase):
  18      """
  19      The main class of TinyDB.
  20  
  21      The ``TinyDB`` class is responsible for creating the storage class instance
  22      that will store this database's documents, managing the database
  23      tables as well as providing access to the default table.
  24  
  25      For table management, a simple ``dict`` is used that stores the table class
  26      instances accessible using their table name.
  27  
  28      Default table access is provided by forwarding all unknown method calls
  29      and property access operations to the default table by implementing
  30      ``__getattr__``.
  31  
  32      When creating a new instance, all arguments and keyword arguments (except
  33      for ``storage``) will be passed to the storage class that is provided. If
  34      no storage class is specified, :class:`~tinydb.storages.JSONStorage` will be
  35      used.
  36  
  37      .. admonition:: Customization
  38  
  39          For customization, the following class variables can be set:
  40  
  41          - ``table_class`` defines the class that is used to create tables,
  42          - ``default_table_name`` defines the name of the default table, and
  43          - ``default_storage_class`` will define the class that will be used to
  44            create storage instances if no other storage is passed.
  45  
  46          .. versionadded:: 4.0
  47  
  48      .. admonition:: Data Storage Model
  49  
  50          Data is stored using a storage class that provides persistence for a
  51          ``dict`` instance. This ``dict`` contains all tables and their data.
  52          The data is modelled like this::
  53  
  54              {
  55                  'table1': {
  56                      0: {document...},
  57                      1: {document...},
  58                  },
  59                  'table2': {
  60                      ...
  61                  }
  62              }
  63  
  64          Each entry in this ``dict`` uses the table name as its key and a
  65          ``dict`` of documents as its value. The document ``dict`` contains
  66          document IDs as keys and the documents themselves as values.
  67  
  68      :param storage: The class of the storage to use. Will be initialized
  69                      with ``args`` and ``kwargs``.
  70      """
  71  
  72      #: The class that will be used to create table instances
  73      #:
  74      #: .. versionadded:: 4.0
  75      table_class = Table
  76  
  77      #: The name of the default table
  78      #:
  79      #: .. versionadded:: 4.0
  80      default_table_name = '_default'
  81  
  82      #: The class that will be used by default to create storage instances
  83      #:
  84      #: .. versionadded:: 4.0
  85      default_storage_class = JSONStorage
  86  
  87      def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
  88          """
  89          Create a new instance of TinyDB.
  90          """
  91  
  92          storage = kwargs.pop('storage', self.default_storage_class)
  93  
  94          # Prepare the storage
  95          self._storage: Storage = storage(*args, **kwargs)
  96  
  97          self._opened = True
  98          self._tables: dict[str, Table] = {}
  99  
 100      def __repr__(self):
 101  
 102          args = [
 103              f'tables={list(self.tables())}',
 104              f'tables_count={len(self.tables())}',
 105              f'default_table_documents_count={self.__len__()}',
 106              f'all_tables_documents_count={[f"{table}={len(self.table(table))}" for table in self.tables()]}',
 107          ]
 108  
 109          return '<{} {}>'.format(type(self).__name__, ', '.join(args))
 110  
 111      def table(self, name: str, **kwargs) -> Table:
 112          """
 113          Get access to a specific table.
 114  
 115          If the table hasn't been accessed yet, a new table instance will be
 116          created using the :attr:`~tinydb.database.TinyDB.table_class` class.
 117          Otherwise, the previously created table instance will be returned.
 118  
 119          All further options besides the name are passed to the table class which
 120          by default is :class:`~tinydb.table.Table`. Check its documentation
 121          for further parameters you can pass.
 122  
 123          :param name: The name of the table.
 124          :param kwargs: Keyword arguments to pass to the table class constructor
 125          """
 126  
 127          if name in self._tables:
 128              return self._tables[name]
 129  
 130          table = self.table_class(self.storage, name, **kwargs)
 131          self._tables[name] = table
 132  
 133          return table
 134  
 135      def tables(self) -> set[str]:
 136          """
 137          Get the names of all tables in the database.
 138  
 139          :returns: a set of table names
 140          """
 141  
 142          # TinyDB stores data as a dict of tables like this:
 143          #
 144          #   {
 145          #       '_default': {
 146          #           0: {document...},
 147          #           1: {document...},
 148          #       },
 149          #       'table1': {
 150          #           ...
 151          #       }
 152          #   }
 153          #
 154          # To get a set of table names, we thus construct a set of this main
 155          # dict which returns a set of the dict keys which are the table names.
 156          #
 157          # Storage.read() may return ``None`` if the database file is empty,
 158          # so we need to consider this case to and return an empty set in this
 159          # case.
 160  
 161          return set(self.storage.read() or {})
 162  
 163      def drop_tables(self) -> None:
 164          """
 165          Drop all tables from the database. **CANNOT BE REVERSED!**
 166          """
 167  
 168          # We drop all tables from this database by writing an empty dict
 169          # to the storage thereby returning to the initial state with no tables.
 170          self.storage.write({})
 171  
 172          # After that we need to remember to empty the ``_tables`` dict, so we'll
 173          # create new table instances when a table is accessed again.
 174          self._tables.clear()
 175  
 176      def drop_table(self, name: str) -> None:
 177          """
 178          Drop a specific table from the database. **CANNOT BE REVERSED!**
 179  
 180          :param name: The name of the table to drop.
 181          """
 182  
 183          # If the table is currently opened, we need to forget the table class
 184          # instance
 185          if name in self._tables:
 186              del self._tables[name]
 187  
 188          data = self.storage.read()
 189  
 190          # The database is uninitialized, there's nothing to do
 191          if data is None:
 192              return
 193  
 194          # The table does not exist, there's nothing to do
 195          if name not in data:
 196              return
 197  
 198          # Remove the table from the data dict
 199          del data[name]
 200  
 201          # Store the updated data back to the storage
 202          self.storage.write(data)
